correctness.rationale: All distances other than the two endpoints are unchanged by one edge fault. The lost-edge link is two cliques joined by n-1 rungs, so its integral H1 has a basis of n-2 four-cycles. The pair relative H3 is that free lattice, and coordinate three-subcube cross-polytope spheres map onto its primitive basis. The exact sequence, simple connectivity of the edge-star intersection, Hurewicz, and Whitehead establish an integral wedge of c_n-(n-2) 3-spheres for every n>=3. The formula for c_n is the explicitly inspected Adamaszek-Adams theorem. The persistence comparison uses the Adams-Virk nullhomotopy of consecutive intact-cube Rips inclusions. Standalone BFS and GF(2) chain checks of n=3..6 independently match all indicated finite ranks. The computations are not the all-dimensional proof.

value.rationale: The source-motivated question asks how robust the Hamming-cube Rips topology is to removing a single graph connection and recomputing all metric distances. For every cube dimension, the exact loss is one circle at radius 1 and n-2 integral 3-sphere summands at radius 2, with all remaining barcode intervals unchanged. The nontrivial primitive edge-link computation explains the dimension-dependent response. This is a natural infinite-family stability classification, not a textbook renaming, arbitrary slice or numerical-only count.
